explanation: Repeatedly remove vertices with no incoming edges. An acyclic directed graph eventually loses every vertex. If vertices remain, each has an incoming edge within the remainder, which implies a directed cycle.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Removing an indegree-zero vertex cannot remove a directed cycle, since each cycle vertex has an incoming cycle edge. A DAG always has an indegree-zero vertex in every nonempty remainder. Thus all vertices are removed exactly when no directed cycle exists.
walkthrough: For edges 0→1, 1→2 and 2→0, every vertex has indegree one. The initial ready queue is empty, so none of the three vertices can be removed and the answer is true.
edgeCases: All disconnected components must be considered.
Duplicate edges increment and decrement indegrees consistently.
